If \(p \neq 3\), then since \(p\) is prime, \(p \equiv \pm 1 \pmod 3\), so \(p^2 \equiv 1 \pmod 3\). Thus
\[
8p^2+1 \equiv 8(1)+1 = 9 \equiv 0 \pmod 3.
\]
Since \(8p^2+1>3\), it is composite, contradicting the hypothesis. Hence \(p=3\).

For \(p=3\),
\[
8p^2-p+2 = 8(9)-3+2 = 72-1 = 71,
\]
which is prime.

\[
\boxed{71}
\]
